look_here_first: Colony-forming woodland sedge with broad leaves and several long drooping pistillate spikes below a raised cluster of staminate spikes.

key_traits.label: Family pattern
key_traits.text: Cyperaceae/Carex: grasslike sedges with sheathing leaves; the fruit is enclosed in a perigynium, and perigynium shape/beak/venation are often decisive for species ID.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: leaf blades relatively broad, about 2.5–7 mm

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: proximal pistillate spikes arching or drooping

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: staminate spikes conspicuously raised above pistillate spikes

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: mesic forest, floodplain, streambank and calcareous woodland habitat

lookalikes.differences: Among these five, C. cherokeensis is the broad-leaved drooping-spike woodland sedge. It is much taller and looser than C. texensis and lacks the silvery winged perigynia of C. tetrastachya.
